title: Fluid ingestion attenuates the decline in VO2peak associated with cardiovascular drift
authors: Ganio MS, Wingo JE, Carroll CE, Thomas MK, Cureton KJ
population: Eleven trained men cycling at 60% control VO2max in 30 C, 40% relative humidity
findings: VO2peak was measured immediately after 15, 60 or 120 min without fluid (15 NF, 60 NF, 120 NF) or after 120 min with fluid (120 F); body mass fell 0.7, 2.3 and 3.7% in 120 F, 60 NF and 120 NF.
Stroke volume and VO2peak fell significantly from 15-min values in 120 NF (13.8% and 8.7%) but not in 60 NF (4.6% and 1.2%) or 120 F (2.1% and 1.9%).
Authors conclude the progressive stroke-volume decline reduces VO2peak and that fluid ingestion mitigates it.
limitations: Eleven trained men, cycling, 30 C only; the stroke-volume decline cannot be separated from dehydration and hyperthermia in the abstract; running not tested.
implications: Dehydration of roughly 3-4% body mass over 2 h in the warm was accompanied by a large drop in VO2peak (about 9%), while about 0.7% loss with fluid was not; use about 2% body-mass loss as a conservative flag for excluding a run from durability estimates (the exact cut-off is not established).
Fluid intake in long warm runs is a plan-level instruction, not only a race-day tip.
